result.title: RoboProbe: Benchmarking Physical Plausibility of Robot World Models
result.summary: Evaluating the physical plausibility of generated videos is critical for reliable robotic planning with world models. These videos inform action proposal and assessment before real-world execution, so undetected physical violations can lead to erroneous assessments of action feasibility and safety. Yet current video generators often produce physically implausible interactions. Detecting such violations directly with vision-language models (VLMs) remains challenging as physical verification requires evidence-grounded spatiotemporal reasoning beyond high-level semantic understanding. We develop five law-specific metrics for evaluating physical plausibility by combining spatiotemporal evidence from segmentation, tracking, 3D geometry, or appearance comparisons with targeted VLM reasoning: Contact fidelity, Object persistence, Solidity, Robot deformation, and Object deformation. Building on this metric suite, we introduce RoboProbe, an agentic evaluation framework that coordinates metric execution and selectively refines evaluations through constrained actions. To evaluate the physical plausibility of robot world models, we further introduce RP-Bench, with 761 human-labeled generated videos and 130 real demonstrations of 239 manipulation tasks from 12 robot datasets. On RP-Bench, all five metrics achieve AUROCs above 0.85 and outperform the evaluated learned judges, prior evaluators, and a frames-only Gemini baseline. Applying these metrics to five video generators reveals distinct patterns of physical violations across models, in both violation types and frequencies.

AI.brief_summary: 该文面向机器人世界模型生成的视频，提出五个「物理规律专项」指标（接触真实性、客体持续性、固体性、机器人形变、客体形变），把分割、跟踪、3D 几何与外观对比得到的时空证据与 VLM 推理结合，并构建由 agentic 框架协调指标执行、通过受限动作选择性精化的评测流程，同时发布含人工标注的 RP-Bench。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先采集时空证据再定向调用 VLM 推理、并按需受限精化」的评测框架，可供核查多模态推理中的视觉证据筛选与 LOOK/STOP 成本收益，但论文本身研究视频物理可信度评测，并非 latent 推理机制。
